static_findings.snippet: | Tool calls | `tool_calls` array | Content blocks | `functionCall` in parts |
| Function calling API | Native `tools` parameter | OpenAI, Anthropic |
| `auto` | Model decides whether to call tools | General usage |
| `required` | Model must call at least one tool | Force tool use |
| `none` | Model cannot call tools | Planning phase |
| `{"function": {"name": "X"}}` | Model must call specific tool | Guided execution |
| `token` | Text fragment | Emit to UI, accumulate |

content.value_statement: Agent frameworks hide complex provider protocol differences. This skill helps teams document message formats, tool calls, streaming behavior, and adapter choices.
actual_capabilities: Maps OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and custom message formats.
Explains how tool schemas and tool results move across provider APIs.
Documents streaming events, partial tool calls, and accumulator patterns.
Identifies system prompt, scratchpad, interrupt, and conversation state patterns.
Compares adapter, gateway, and unified client abstraction strategies.
Produces a structured markdown report for framework protocol analysis.
limitations: Does not execute framework code or verify runtime behavior by itself.
Requires access to relevant source files and line references.
Does not replace provider documentation or API changelog review.
May need companion skills for tool registration or memory orchestration details.

use_cases.title: Document Provider Message Translation
use_cases.description: Map how internal messages become provider requests and how responses return to the framework.

use_cases.title: Audit Streaming Tool Calls
use_cases.description: Review how partial tool arguments are accumulated, parsed, and delivered to downstream handlers.

use_cases.title: Compare Agent Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Compare adapters, gateways, and unified clients before designing a new LLM abstraction layer.

prompt_templates.title: Map Message Formats
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a small framework or provider module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the message protocol for this framework. Identify internal roles, provider request formats, and response conversion points.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Tool Calls
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after finding tool registration and execution files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace how tool schemas reach the model and how tool calls return. Include file references and note parser behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Streaming Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the framework supports token streaming or streamed tool calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the streaming protocol. Focus on event types, partial tool argument handling, completion signals, and error behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Provider Abstractions
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced architecture review across multiple providers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the provider abstraction strategy. Explain adapter boundaries, feature gaps, graceful degradation, and implications for new framework design.

output_examples.input: A framework supports OpenAI and Anthropic adapters.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the shared internal message type, the provider-specific request conversion, and the response normalization path.

output_examples.input: A streaming handler receives partial tool arguments.
output_examples.output: The report explains the accumulator pattern, completion event, error path, and the point where arguments become executable tool calls.

output_examples.input: A team is choosing between a gateway and thin adapters.
output_examples.output: The report compares ownership boundaries, provider feature loss, test surface, and long-term maintenance tradeoffs.

best_practices: Start with message types before reading provider adapters.
Cite file paths and line numbers for every protocol claim.
Separate wire format findings from tool execution behavior.
anti_patterns: Treating all providers as OpenAI-compatible without checking translation code.
Ignoring streaming edge cases around partial tool arguments.
Documenting prompts without distinguishing framework prompts from user data.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes the boundary between agent framework logic and model provider APIs.

faq.question: Does it cover tool registration?
faq.answer: It focuses on wire encoding and parsing. Tool registration is better handled by a tool interface analysis.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple LLM providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes comparison points for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, local models, and custom adapters.

faq.question: Does it require running the framework?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for source review, but runtime tests can strengthen the conclusions.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a structured markdown report with protocol findings, tables, code references, and architecture implications.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for framework maintainers, AI platform engineers, and architecture reviewers.
